title: Let George Do It
paragraphs: Bob Bailey stars as George Valentine, a resourceful troubleshooter who answers requests for help and repeatedly finds ordinary jobs turning into mysteries, danger, and murder.
West Coast mystery/private-detective drama developed from a classified-ad troubleshooter premise. Early material is lighter and comic; the series evolves into a tougher crime drama.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Development / auditions (1946-04 to May 14, 1946), Early light mystery/comedy phase (October 4, 1946 to December 31, 1948) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Mature Bob Bailey private-eye phase (January 1, 1949 to November 29, 1953) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and Olan Soule final phase (November 30, 1953 to September 27, 1954) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|bob-bailey|Bob Bailey]] (performer), Bud Hiestand (announcer), Eddie Dunstedter (composer, conductor, and presenter), David Victor (writer), Don Clark (director), [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]] (performer), and Jackson Gillis (writer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]], [[org|org.3a48199732c67e6f|KFRC]], and [[org|org.87e6f64937f0bfb8|KHJ]].
The stories often return to murder and homicide, private investigation, theft, robbery and stolen property, missing persons, travel and distant locations, and wartime service and veteran connections.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar veteran-to-private-investigator setting, West Coast regional network detective production, Standard Oil / Chevron sponsorship, and New York transcription distribution.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], and [[show|escape|Escape]].
